# Resource: stripe_tax_rate

A rate of tax that invoices and subscriptions apply. `terraform destroy` archives the tax rate, because Stripe cannot delete one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "stripe_tax_rate" "vat" {
  display_name = "VAT"
  description  = "UK VAT"
  jurisdiction = "GB"
  country      = "GB"
  percentage   = 20
  inclusive    = false
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `display_name` - (Required) The display name of the tax rate, which will be shown to users.
* `inclusive` - (Required) This specifies if the tax rate is inclusive or exclusive. Changing it replaces the resource.
* `percentage` - (Required) This represents the tax rate percent out of 100. Changing it replaces the resource.

The following arguments are optional:

* `active` - (Optional) Flag determining whether the tax rate is active or inactive (archived). Inactive tax rates cannot be used with new applications or Checkout Sessions, but will still work for subscriptions and invoices that already have it set. Removing it from the configuration stops sending it, and the next apply records the value Stripe holds.
* `country` - (Optional) Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `description` - (Optional) An arbitrary string attached to the tax rate for your internal use only. It will not be visible to your customers.
* `jurisdiction` - (Optional) The jurisdiction for the tax rate. You can use this label field for tax reporting purposes. It also appears on your customer’s invoice.
* `metadata` - (Optional) Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `state` - (Optional) [ISO 3166-2 subdivision code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2), without country prefix. For example, "NY" for New York, United States.
* `tax_type` - (Optional) The high-level tax type, such as `vat` or `sales_tax`. Possible values: `amusement_tax`, `communications_tax`, `digital_excise_tax`, `gst`, `hst`, `igst`, `jct`, `lease_tax`, `mass_transit_parking_tax`, `parking_tax`, `pst`, `qst`, `retail_delivery_fee`, `rst`, `sales_tax`, `service_tax`, `utility_users_tax`, `vat`.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `effective_percentage` - Actual/effective tax rate percentage out of 100. For tax calculations with automatic_tax[enabled]=true, this percentage reflects the rate actually used to calculate tax based on the product's taxability and whether the user is registered to collect taxes in the corresponding jurisdiction.
* `flat_amount` - The amount of the tax rate when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. Tax rates with `rate_type` `percentage` can vary based on the transaction, resulting in this field being `null`. This field exposes the amount and currency of the flat tax rate. See [`flat_amount`](#flat_amount) below.
* `jurisdiction_level` - The level of the jurisdiction that imposes this tax rate. Will be `null` for manually defined tax rates. Possible values: `city`, `country`, `county`, `district`, `multiple`, `state`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `rate_type` - Indicates the type of tax rate applied to the taxable amount. This value can be `null` when no tax applies to the location. This field is only present for TaxRates created by Stripe Tax. Possible values: `flat_amount`, `percentage`.

<a id="flat_amount"></a>
### `flat_amount`

The `flat_amount` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount of the tax when the `rate_type` is `flat_amount`. This positive integer represents how much to charge in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).
* `currency` - Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a tax rate using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_tax_rate.vat
  id = "txr_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = stripe_tax_rate.vat
  identity = {
    id = "txr_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the tax rate.

Using `terraform import`, import a tax rate using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import stripe_tax_rate.vat txr_123
```
